# Dataset values are injected by the server, never generated by the model

When a journalist attaches a spreadsheet, the model sees only its schema and a few sample rows. When a version is created, the server parses the full file and injects it verbatim into the HTML as `<script type="application/json" id="embed-data">`, and the model writes code that reads from that block. A model retyping figures can silently change them, and in journalism a wrong number in front of readers is worse than a missing feature. This also keeps prompt size independent of dataset size. The trade-off is that the model must write data-driven code rather than hardcoding values, and that datasets are limited to a few thousand rows.

## Amendment: one marker per dataset

The data goes into a marker per dataset, not a single `id="embed-data"` block, so an embed can combine several datasets. The model writes an empty `<script type="application/json" data-dataset="ID"></script>`, and the server fills it when the version is created.
- **Escaping.** Every `<` in the data is escaped as `<`, so no cell can end the script.
- **Unknown marker.** A marker naming a dataset that doesn't exist is a broken reply, and creates no version.
- **What the model sees.** When the version is shown back to the model, the markers are emptied again, so it never sees, and so can't retype, the full figures.
- **Quality check.** The check runs on that same emptied document, because a dataset's cells are data, not code.
